verses.zh: 这是我第三次要到你们那里去。「凭两三个人的口作见证，句句都要定准。」
verses.en: This is the third time I am coming to visit[NOTE:1] you. By the testimony[NOTE:2] of two or three witnesses every matter will be established.[NOTE:3]
notes: The word “visit” is not in the Greek text, but is implied.
A quotation from Deut 19:15 (also quoted in Matt 18:16; 1 Tim 5:19).
verses.commentary:
13:1 "This is the third time I am coming to you" This gives textual credence to the theory of
Paul's painful visit to Corinth between the writing of I and 2 Corinthians (cf. 2 Cor. 12:14). This
visit is not recorded in the book of Acts. See Introduction, III.

▣ "every fact" This begins a quote from Deut. 19:15
(cf. Num. 35:30; Deut. 17:6; also quoted in Matt. 18:16; 1 Tim. 5:19), which deals with court procedures. To what
does it refer in this chapter? There are two possibilities.

- It refers to the church's evaluation of Paul. He had been there twice and shared with them. They
were responsible and would be held accountable as hearers of the truth.

- It refers to church discipline related to a group within the church.

- the factious groups of 1 Cor. 1-4 (cf. 2 Cor. 12:20)

- an immoral group (cf. 2 Cor. 12:21)

- the "super apostles" or false teachers with connections to Jerusalem and Judaism
(chapters 10-13, especially 11:13-15)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH DISCIPLINE

NASB
"is to be confirmed"

NKJV, REB
"shall be established"

NRSV, Peshitta
"must be sustained"

TEV
"must be upheld"

NJB
"is required"

The form of this VERB is a FUTURE PASSIVE INDICATIVE
(cf. NKJV), but Barbara and Timothy Friberg, Analytical Greek New Testament, p. 573, say it
is functioning as an AORIST PASSIVE IMPERATIVE (cf. NRSV, NJB).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STAND (histēmi)

verses.zh: 我从前说过，如今不在你们那里又说，正如我第二次见你们的时候所说的一样，就是对那犯了罪的和其余的人说：「我若再来，必不宽容。」
verses.en: I said before when I was present the second time and now, though absent, I say again to those who sinned previously and to all the rest, that if I come again, I will not spare anyone,[NOTE:1]
notes: The word “anyone” is not in the Greek text but is implied.
verses.commentary:
13:2 "those who have sinned in the past and all the rest as well" This seems to relate to
two groups. The first "who have sinned in the past" (PERFECT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE), must
refer to those believers at Corinth who heard Paul twice, but still rebelled against his leadership.
This would be the factious groups of 1 Corinthians 1-4 or an immoral group (cf. 2 Cor. 12:20-21;
1 Corinthians 5).

The phrase "and all the rest" seems to relate to those who were not
present both times, possibly the false apostles from Jerusalem and their supporters, which are the
focus of chapters 10-13. However, both groups/all groups are put on notice that Paul wants them to
deal with the problems, but if they do not, he will!

▣ "if" This is a THIRD CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE, but it is used in
the sense of "when" (cf. John 16:7 and 1 John 3:2).

▣ "I will not spare anyone" Paul uses this term in a positive sense in 1 Cor. 7:23
and 2 Cor. 1:23, but in a judicial sense both here and in 2 Cor. 12:6 (cf. 2 Cor. 10:11).

verses.zh: 你们既然寻求基督在我里面说话的凭据，我必不宽容。因为，基督在你们身上不是软弱的，在你们里面是有大能的。
verses.en: since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He[NOTE:1] is not weak toward you but is powerful among you.
notes: Grk “who.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
verses.commentary:
13:3 "proof" This concept of testing is recurrent in this context. There is a sustained word
play between the connotations of two Greek terms, dokimazō and peirazō.

- v. 3, proof ‒ dokimē (cf. 2 Cor. 2:9; 8:2; 9:13; 13:3)

- v. 5, test ‒ peirazō (cf. 2 Cor. 13:5)

- v. 5, examine ‒ dokimazō (cf. 2 Cor. 8:8,22; 13:5)

- v. 5, fail the test ‒ adokimos

- v. 6, do not fail the test ‒ adokimos

- v. 7, approve ‒ dokimos (cf. 2 Cor. 10:18)

- v. 7, unapprove ‒ adokimos

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK TERMS FOR TESTING AND THEIR CONNOTATIONS

▣ "of the Christ who speaks in me" Some at Corinth were challenging Paul's authority.
They were "testing" Paul! In 2 Cor. 13:5 Paul will "test" them! Christ's presence in Paul had
been confirmed (cf. 2 Cor. 12:12).

▣ "is not weak" Weakness is God's way to victory as illustrated in Jesus' life
(cf. 2 Cor. 13:4) and Paul's life (cf. 2 Cor. 10:1,11; 12:9; 13:9). No human being will glory before God for spiritual accomplishments
that are a direct result of who God is and not who we are (cf. 1 Cor. 1:29; Eph. 2:8-9). It is God's resources which accomplish spiritual
results! Believers must allow His power to flow through their need and helplessness. The Christian life is a divine gift, as is salvation,
but it must be received and maintained by the believer.

Verses 3-4 are the summary antithesis of the rhetorically arrogant false teachers. They
claimed a superiority from

- racial lineage

- personal charismatic experience

- superior Sophistic, rhetorical training

- personal comparisons

▣ "toward you. . .in you" This PLURAL "you" shows that Paul is referring
to a congregational experience, not personal experience (cf. 2 Cor. 13:5). Possibly the TEV translation,
"among you," catches the flavor.

verses.zh: 他因软弱被钉在十字架上，却因　神的大能仍然活着。我们也是这样同他软弱，但因　神向你们所显的大能，也必与他同活。
verses.en: For indeed he was crucified by reason of weakness, but he lives because of God’s power. For we also are weak in him, but we will live together with him, because of God’s power toward you.
verses.commentary:
13:4 "crucified" Paul uses several terms to describe Jesus' death:

- death (cf. Rom. 5:6ff; 8:34; 14:15; 1 Cor. 8:11; 15:3; 2 Cor. 5:15; Gal. 2:21;
1 Thess. 4:14; 5:10)

- blood (cf. Rom. 3:25; 5:9; Eph. 1:7; 2:13; Col. 1:20)

- cross (cf. 1 Cor.1:17-18; Gal. 5:11; 6:12,14; Eph. 2:16; Phil. 2:8; Col. 1:20; 2:14)

- crucifixion (cf. 1 Cor. 1:23; 2:2; 2 Cor. 13:14; Gal. 3:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CRUCIFIXION

▣ "yet He lives because of the power of God" It is phrases like this that caused so many
Christological controversies in the early church. Is not Jesus God also? Does the human Jesus live
by the power of a separate deity (i.e., YHWH)? One cannot build a systematic understanding on one
verse or selected verses, but must try to unify all of the theological concepts into an integrated
whole.

Usually the terminology of this verse is used to affirm that God the Father, as an
act of approval, raised the Son (cf. Acts 2:24; 3:15; 4:10; 5:30; 10:40; 13:30,33,34,37; 17:31;
Rom. 1:4; 6:4,9; 8:11; 10:9; 1 Cor. 6:14; 2 Cor. 4:14; Gal. 1:1; Eph. 1:20; Col. 2:12; 1 Thess. 1:10).
However, there are other inspired texts that affirm that

- the Spirit raised the Son (cf. Rom. 8:11)

- the Son raised Himself (cf. John 2:19-22; 10:17-18)

▣ "we also are weak in Him, yet we will live with Him" Paul's understanding of Christianity
was an identification of the believers in the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus. As He lived a
humble, gentle, and misunderstood life, so will we; as He died in service to others, so should we (cf. 1 John 3:16); as
He was raised, so are we (i.e., new life now) and will be (i.e., resurrection body at the Second Coming).

This identification theology is so evident in Romans 6. Paul wrote Romans while he was
dealing with Corinth. Paul's systematic understanding of Christianity (i.e., Romans) was fleshed out
while he was working with this dysfunctional church.

verses.zh: 你们总要自己省察有信心没有，也要自己试验。岂不知你们若不是可弃绝的，就有耶稣基督在你们心里吗？
verses.en: Put yourselves to the test to see if you are in the faith; examine yourselves! Or do you not recognize regarding yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you—unless, indeed, you fail the test![NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
13:5 "Test yourselves" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE. This is the
word peirazō, which means "to test with a view toward destruction." See full note at
1 Cor. 3:13. They had tested Paul; now they must be tested themselves!

▣ "if" This is a FIRST CLASS COONDITIONAL SENTENCE which is assumed
to be true. Paul is not doubting their faith, but challenging them to wake up!

▣ "the faith" The Greek term "faith" (pistis) is translated into English by
three terms: faith, believe, or trust. Faith is used in three senses in the NT:

- as personal acceptance of Jesus as the Christ of God

- as faithfully living for Him

- as a body of truths about Him (cf. 2 Cor. 13:3; Gal. 1:23; 3:23-25)

Mature Christianity involves all three senses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

▣ "examine yourselves" Paul repeats his command (i.e., another PRESENT ACTIVE
IMPERATIVE), but uses the other term (i.e., dokimazō) for testing, which implies
to test with a view toward approval.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK TERMS FOR TESTING AND THEIR CONNOTATIONS

▣ "recognize" This is the Greek term epigniōskō (i.e., PRESENT
ACTIVE INDICATIVE), which usually denotes experiential full knowledge.

▣ "Jesus Christ is in you" As 2 Cor. 13:4 focused on the corporate aspect, this phrase
(using the same PREPOSITION and PLURAAL PRONOUN) may refer to a more
individual aspect. Christ is surely among His people, but also in each of His people!

The ministries of Jesus and the Spirit are so closely linked that often the Spirit is called the Spirit of Christ
(cf. Rom. 8:9; 1 Pet. 1:11). Jesus is even said to indwell believers (cf. John 14:23; Rom. 8:10;
Col. 1:27. Also notice Matt. 28:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS AND THE SPIRIT

▣ "unless indeed you fail the test" This phrase is parallel to "if you are in the faith"
in 2 Cor. 13:5. Paul has asserted in several ways (i.e., FIRST CLASS CONDITIONAL SENTENCE
in 2 Cor. 13:5 and the use of dokimazō) that he believes his readers are believers, but
not all of them. There is a contingent of false teachers who do not know Christ. This clause relates
to them.

This clause does not relate to sinful believers because Paul addresses them in
2 Cor. 12:20-21. They need to repent, but the false teachers need to be saved by faith in Christ alone (cf Matt. 7).

Paul used this very same term in 1 Cor. 9:27 as the reason why he struggled to keep
himself under God's control. Paul did not want to be "disqualified" or rejected (see A. T. Robertson, Word Pictures
in the NT, vol. 4, p. 150). Believers are challenged to check up on themselves (cf. Phil. 2:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY

verses.zh: 我却盼望你们晓得，我们不是可弃绝的人。
verses.en: And I hope that you will realize that we have not failed the test![NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
13:6 Paul is asserting that he and his helpers have passed the test (i.e., not counterfeits,
adokimos, cf. 2 Cor. 13:7), especially in relation to the church at Corinth. If they have
the indwelling Christ, this is evidence that Paul's ministry was effective.

verses.zh: 我们求　神，叫你们一件恶事都不做；这不是要显明我们是蒙悦纳的，是要你们行事端正，任凭人看我们是被弃绝的吧！
verses.en: Now we pray to God that you may not do anything wrong, not so that we may appear to have passed the test,[NOTE:1] but so that you may do what is right[NOTE:2] even if we may appear to have failed the test.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “that we may appear to be approved.”
verses.commentary:
13:7 In a sense a strong, orthodox Corinthian church would affirm Paul's leadership and
Apostolic credentials. He is more concerned that they do what is right and appropriate because
of God and the gospel, not just to show Paul's credentials or affirm his leadership (cf. 2 Cor. 13:9).

▣ "approved. . .unapproved" Paul continues this word play on dokimos and
adokimos.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK TERMS FOR TESTING AND THEIR CONNOTATIONS

verses.zh: 我们凡事不能敌挡真理，只能扶助真理。
verses.en: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the sake of the truth.
verses.commentary:
13:8 The truth in this context refers to the gospel as a person (i.e., Jesus the Messiah), as
a message (i.e., the gospel about Jesus), and as a lifestyle (i.e., emulation of Jesus' life).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "TRUTH" IN PAUL'S WRITINGS

verses.zh: 即使我们软弱，你们刚强，我们也欢喜；并且我们所求的，就是你们作完全人。
verses.en: For we rejoice whenever we are weak, but you are strong. And we pray for this: that you may become fully qualified.[NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
13:9 "we rejoice when we ourselves are weak but you are strong" This is Paul's paradox. He
knows that spiritual power is released through human weakness (cf. 2 Cor. 12:10; 13:4). Therefore,
he wants to remain weak. However, for the Corinthian church to be strong, she too, must become weak.
This is so opposite of the way they evaluated life. The false teachers have asserted strength
through education, lineage, experience, but Paul asserts strength through Christ's example
(cf. 2 Cor. 13:4).

▣ "that you be made complete" The NOUN form of this term is found only
here in the NT. The VERB means "to knit together." Paul used the VERB form
in 1 Cor. 1:10, which calls on the Corinthian church to end its factious divisions. Now at the end
of 2 Corinthians he returns to this mandate (i.e., unity which will result in spiritual adequacies).

Louw and Nida, Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament, vol. 1, p. 680, asserts
that artios (i.e., complete, adequate, fully equipped for the assigned task), with all its
different prepositional compounds (i.e., epi and kata), are all synonyms (cf. Luke 6:40;
2 Cor. 13:9,11; Eph. 4:12; 2 Tim. 3:17).

Paul wants a functioning, unified, loving church in Corinth (cf. 2 Cor. 13:11). For this
to occur there must be forgiveness, reconciliation, and church discipline (cf. Gal. 6:1).

verses.zh: 所以，我不在你们那里的时候，把这话写给你们，好叫我见你们的时候，不用照主所给我的权柄严厉地待你们。这权柄原是为造就人，并不是为败坏人。
verses.en: Because of this I am writing these things while absent, so that when I arrive[NOTE:1] I may not have to deal harshly with you[NOTE:2] by using my authority—the Lord gave it to me for building up, not for tearing down!
notes: Grk “when I am present,” but in the context of Paul’s third (upcoming) visit to Corinth, this is better translated as “when I arrive.”
The words “with you” are not in the Greek text, but are implied.
verses.commentary:
13:10 Paul did not want to make another painful visit to Corinth (cf. 2 Cor. 2:3-4). He did not
want to come wrapped in his Apostolic authority, but in parental love. However, the response of the
church determined how he must act.

▣ "with the authority which the Lord gave me" This exact phrase appears in 2 Cor. 10:8.
This Apostolic authority, whether in personal presence or from afar (cf. 1 Cor. 5:4), has Christ's
authority (cf. 2 Cor. 12:19; 13:3). This authority was given to Paul in the Damascus road encounter
(cf. Acts 9; 22; 26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: AUTHORITY (exousia)

▣ "building up" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: EDIFY

verses.zh: 还有末了的话：愿弟兄们都喜乐。要作完全人；要受安慰；要同心合意；要彼此和睦。如此，仁爱和平的　神必常与你们同在。
verses.en: Finally, brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] rejoice, set things right, be encouraged, agree with one another, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:8.
verses.commentary:
13:11 "Finally" Literally this is "for the rest" (cf. Gal. 6:17). This is a characteristic
concluding phrase for Paul (cf. Eph. 6:10; Phil. 3:1; 4:8; 2 Thess. 3:1). It usually marks a transition
to a closing point.

▣ "brethren" What a beautiful and comforting way to close this difficult letter to a
problem church. It also functions as a literary device to signal the transition to a new subject.

▣ There is a series of five PRESENT IMPERATIVES.

- "rejoice" (PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE). Paul often uses this term in 2 Corinthians
(cf. 2 Cor. 2:3; 6:10; 7:7,9,13,16; 13:9,11). This term can mean "good bye" (cf. Phil. 3:1; 4:4),
but this does not fit a series of IMPERATIVES.

- "be made complete" (PRESENT PASSIVE IMPERATIVE). This speaks of unity and
service (cf. v 9).

- "be comforted" (PRESENT PASSIVE IMPERATIVE). Paul uses this term often in
2 Corinthians (cf. 2 Cor. 1:4,6; 2:7,8; 5:20; 6:1; 7:6,7,13; 8:6; 9:5; 10:1; 12:8,18; 13:11).

- "be like-minded" (PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE). This Greek term has many
connotations (cf. Louw and Nida, vol. 2, p. 259), but in this context it is parallel to
"be made complete." This refers to unity for the sake of the gospel. This is not asserting
that believers must agree about every issue, but that they must disagree in love and that
the gospel should always have priority over personal opinions or preferences!

- "live in peace" (PRESENT ACTIVE IMPERATIVE). This surely reflects 1 Corinthians 1-4
and 2 Corinthians 10-13. It is uncertain how these problems relate, but both caused disunity
and contention. Paul commands peace, not by compromise, but by Christlikeness. The God of peace
(cf. 2 Cor. 13:11) will help us in our weakness!

▣ "the God of love and peace" What a wonderful descriptive title for YHWH. YHWH is often
connected with "peace" (cf. Rom. 15:33; 16:20; 1 Cor. 14:33; Phil. 4:9; 1 Thess. 5:23; Heb. 13:20).
He is called the "Lord of peace" in 2 Thess. 3:16. Love and peace are both mentioned in Eph. 6:23.

Believers must emulate these characteristics in their relationships with one another.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DESCRIPTIVE TITLES FOR GOD

verses.zh: 你们亲嘴问安，彼此务要圣洁。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
notes: The versification of vv. 12 and 13 in the NET (so also NRSV, NLT) is according to the versification in the NA28 and UBS5 editions of the Greek text. Some translations, however, break the material up into three verses, i.e., 12-14 (NKJV, NASB, NIV). The same material has been translated in each case; the only difference is the versification of that material.
verses.commentary:
13:12 "Greet" This can be translated "bid farewell" (cf. Acts 20:1; 21:6). It conveys an
attitude of acceptance and cooperation. The opposite attitude is expressed in Matt. 5:47.

Just a comment about the numbering of these last two verses. Some English translations
combine 2 Cor. 13:12-13 (TEV, NJB, RSV, NRSV), while others break it into two verses (KJV, NKJV,
NASB, NIV).

▣ "holy kiss" This custom (i.e., between family members and friends) was later stopped
because of pagan misunderstanding (i.e., erotic kissing). In the early church the men kissed the men
and the women kissed the women (i.e., following the custom of the synagogue, cf. Rom. 16:16; 1 Cor. 16:20;
1 Thess. 5:26). See note at 1 Cor. 16:20.

This is an IMPERATIVE. Does this mean that Christians must greet each
other in this specific manner? Here is a good example of how culture and future situations must affect
interpretation (another good example would be women wearing veils). The form is not the issue, but the
attitude. Believers are a family.

verses.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship[NOTE:1] of the Holy Spirit be with you all.[NOTE:2]
notes: Most witnesses, especially later ones (א2 D Ψ M lat sy bo), conclude this letter with ἀμήν (amēn, “amen”), while several early and significant mss (P46 א* A B F G 0243 6 33 630 1175 1739 1881 sa) lack the particle. Such a conclusion is routinely added by scribes to NT books because a few of these books originally had such an ending (cf. Rom 16:27; Gal 6:18; Jude 25). A majority of Greek witnesses have the concluding ἀμήν in every NT book except Acts, James, and 3 John (and even in these books, ἀμήν is found in some witnesses). It is thus a predictable variant. That so many diverse witnesses lacked the word here is strong testimony to its absence for the original text of 2 Corinthians.
verses.commentary:
13:13 "All the saints" This phrase refers not only to Paul and his missionary team, but "all
the saints" (i.e., all of Paul's other churches). There was a tension between Corinth and these
other churches. There was an air of superiority about this church. Paul addressed this issue by
mentioning several times the standards he taught in all the churches (cf. 1 Cor. 4:17; 7:17; 11:16,34;
14:33). The Corinthian church must be a part of the family, not a privileged, elite member.

In their current crisis, all of the congregations started by Paul sent their greetings,
which implies fellowship, concern, cooperation, prayer, and acceptance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SAINTS

verses.zh: 愿主耶稣基督的恩惠、　神的慈爱、圣灵的感动常与你们众人同在！
verses.commentary:
13:14 Paul always closes his letters in a prayer or benediction, but this one is unique. It
combines three aspects of God's character with the three persons of the Trinity. It is also unusual
that Jesus is mentioned first.

The three aspects of God: grace, love, and fellowship, are for "all" believers at Corinth.
This is a crucial part of the prayer. Paul wants to restore unity among believers yet recognize and
reject false believers.

Paul used a scribe to write his letters, but probably took the pen himself to write
the last prayer personally (cf. 2 Thess. 3:17). Paul loved this church!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

▣ "the fellowship of the Holy Spirit" See notes at 1 Cor. 1:9 and 12:11.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How do believers test themselves?

- Why does Paul speak so often in chapters 11-13 of his weakness?

- How is assurance related to perseverance?

- How can God be one and three at the same time?

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 2 CORINTHIANS 13:1-4

1This is the third time I am coming to you. Every fact is to
be confirmed by the testimony of two or three witnesses. 2I have previously said when present the second time, and though
now absent I say in advance to those who have sinned in the past and to all the rest as well, that if I come again I will not spare anyone,
3since you are seeking for proof of the Christ who speaks in me, and who is not weak toward you, but mighty in you. 4For
indeed He was crucified because of weakness, yet He lives because of the power of God. For we also are weak in Him, yet we will live with Him
because of the power of God directed toward you.
